#!/bin/bash

MYDIR=$(realpath "$(dirname "$0")")
cd "$MYDIR" || exit

HAS_INIT=false
HAS_DETACH=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
  -i | --init)
    HAS_INIT=true
    shift
    ;;
  -d | --detach)
    HAS_DETACH=true
    shift
    ;;
  -q | --quit)
    NITRO_CONTAINERS=$(docker container ls -q --filter name=nitro-testnode)

    if [ -z "$NITRO_CONTAINERS" ]; then
      echo "No nitro-testnode containers running"
    else
      docker container stop $NITRO_CONTAINERS || exit
    fi

    exit 0
    ;;
  *)
    echo "OPTIONS:"
    echo "-i|--init:         clone repo and init nitro test node"
    echo "-d|--detach:       setup nitro test node in detached mode"
    echo "-q|--quit:         shutdown nitro test node docker containers"
    exit 0
    ;;
  esac
done

TEST_NODE_DIR="$MYDIR/../nitro-testnode"
if [ ! -d "$TEST_NODE_DIR" ]; then
  HAS_INIT=true
fi

if $HAS_INIT; then
  cd "$MYDIR" || exit
  cd ..

  git clone -b release --recurse-submodules https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro-testnode.git
  cd ./nitro-testnode || exit
  git checkout c7a58620c431266c90f9d422eca6627e24586e60 || exit

  ./test-node.bash --no-run --init || exit
fi

cd "$TEST_NODE_DIR" || exit
if $HAS_DETACH; then
  ./test-node.bash --detach
else
  ./test-node.bash

#!/bin/bash
set -e

MYDIR=$(realpath "$(dirname "$0")")
cd "$MYDIR"
cd ..

# Optimize contract's wasm binary by crate name.
opt_wasm() {
  local CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME=$1
  local CONTRACT_BIN_NAME="${CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME//-/_}.wasm"
  local CONTRACT_OPT_BIN_NAME="${CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME//-/_}_opt.wasm"

  echo
  echo "Optimizing $CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME WASM binary"
  # https://rustwasm.github.io/book/reference/code-size.html#use-the-wasm-opt-tool
  wasm-opt --enable-bulk-memory -O3 -o ./target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/"$CONTRACT_OPT_BIN_NAME" ./target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/"$CONTRACT_BIN_NAME"
}

# Retrieve all alphanumeric contract's crate names in `./examples` directory.
get_example_crate_names() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC2038
  # NOTE: optimistically relying on the 'name = ' string at Cargo.toml file
  find ./examples -maxdepth 2 -type f -name "Cargo.toml" | xargs grep 'name = ' | grep -oE '".*"' | tr -d "'\""
}

cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
  -Z build-std=std,panic_abort \
  -Z build-std-features=panic_immediate_abort

# Optimize contract's wasm for gas usage.
for CRATE_NAME in $(get_example_crate_names); do
  opt_wasm "$CRATE_NAME"
done

export RPC_URL=http://localhost:8547
export DEPLOYER_ADDRESS=0xcEcba2F1DC234f70Dd89F2041029807F8D03A990

# No need to compile benchmarks with `--release`
# since this only runs the benchmarking code and the contracts have already been compiled with `--release`.
cargo run -p benches
echo "This benchmarks measure gas execution cost,
 the 21000 EVM base gas fee is omitted."
echo
echo "To measure non cached contract's gas usage correctly,
 benchmarks should run on a clean instance of the nitro test node."
echo
echo "Finished running benches!"

#!/bin/bash
set -e

mydir=$(dirname "$0")
cd "$mydir" || exit
cd ..

# Check contract wasm binary by crate name
check_wasm() {
  local CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME=$1
  local CONTRACT_BIN_NAME="${CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME//-/_}.wasm"

  echo
  echo "Checking contract $CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME"
  cargo stylus check -e https://sepolia-rollup.arbitrum.io/rpc --wasm-file ./target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/"$CONTRACT_BIN_NAME"
}

# Retrieve all alphanumeric contract's crate names in `./examples` directory.
get_example_crate_names() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC2038
  # NOTE: optimistically relying on the 'name = ' string at Cargo.toml file
  find ./examples -maxdepth 2 -type f -name "Cargo.toml" | xargs grep -m 1 'name = ' | grep -oE '".*"' | tr -d "'\""
}

cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
  -Z build-std=std,panic_abort \
  -Z build-std-features=panic_immediate_abort

for CRATE_NAME in $(get_example_crate_names); do
  check_wasm "$CRATE_NAME"
  sleep 2
done

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Function to retrieve all Cargo.toml paths in the ./examples directory
get_example_dirs() {
  find ./examples -maxdepth 2 -type f -name "Cargo.toml" | xargs -n1 dirname | sort
}

# Get the root directory of the git repository
ROOT_DIR=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$ROOT_DIR" || exit

# Check contract ABI by crate name
check_abi() {
  local CRATE_PATH=$1

  echo "Checking contract $CRATE_PATH"

  echo

  cd "$CRATE_PATH"

  cargo stylus export-abi

  echo

  echo "Done!"

  echo

  cd "$ROOT_DIR"
}


for CRATE_PATH in $(get_example_dirs); do
  check_abi "$CRATE_PATH"
done

input.description: Inventory v0.3.0 contracts, tests and docs
input.prompt:
You are building a factual inventory of the OpenZeppelin Stylus contracts library at tag v0.3.0, to plan a migration. This is READ-ONLY. The v0.3.0 snapshot is at /tmp/bench/v030 (a git archive of the tag). Do NOT modify it, do not modify /private/tmp/bench/ws, do not run cargo, and do not install anything. Write your deliverable only to /tmp/bench/notes/inventory.md. You may create that directory's files; it already exists.

Facts we already know, so you do not need to re-discover them: the workspace root is /tmp/bench/v030 with members benches, contracts, contracts-proc, lib/crypto, lib/e2e, lib/e2e-proc, plus about 37 crates under examples/ (including examples/basic/token and examples/basic/script). fuzz/ is excluded from the workspace and has its own Cargo.toml with fuzz targets merkle and keccak. templates/crypto-erc20 is also excluded. The docs are Antora AsciiDoc under docs/modules/ROOT/pages/. audits/ holds three PDFs. The `motsu` test framework is used in about 41 .rs files. Global accessors (the stylus_sdk free functions such as msg::sender, block::timestamp and so on) also need inventorying. The E2E framework is in lib/e2e and lib/e2e-proc.

DELIVERABLE: /tmp/bench/notes/inventory.md, with these sections. Use markdown tables where it helps. Be exhaustive and precise: file paths relative to the repo root, and exact identifiers.

1. CRATES AND EXAMPLES. For each workspace member: path, package name, role, dependencies that matter (stylus-sdk, alloy, motsu, e2e, openzeppelin-*), and features. For each example: path, package name, the contract(s) it exposes (the #[entrypoint] struct and its #[public] impls), which library modules it uses, and its test counts (unit, E2E) with file paths.

2. CONTRACTS LIBRARY SHAPE (contracts/src). The module tree. For each public contract, extension, utility and proxy: the main public struct or trait names, and the composition pattern. Say how an extension composes with its base: #[borrow], #[inherit], trait-based overrides, duplicated methods, or something else. Note every place where the composition is awkward or where a method is duplicated or overridden. Give file:line for the key definitions.

3. GLOBAL ACCESSOR CALL SITES. Enumerate every call to a global accessor from stylus_sdk (msg::*, block::*, contract::*, evm::*, call::*, crypto::*, tx::*, storage access that is not through self, and so on). Give a count per file and a list of distinct accessor functions with counts. Include contracts, contracts-proc, lib/crypto, examples, benches, fuzz and lib/e2e*. Grep for patterns such as `msg::`, `block::`, `contract::`, `evm::`, `call::`, `crypto::`, `tx::` and `stylus_sdk::` paths. Be careful: stylus_sdk::alloy_primitives and alloy re-exports are not global accessors. Verify each hit by reading the line.

4. MOTSU TEST INVENTORY. For each .rs file that uses motsu: file path, the number of #[motsu::test] functions, and the motsu API surface used there (Contract::<T>::default(), .sender(...), .msg_value, .block_timestamp, and so on). Give a distinct list of motsu APIs with counts.

5. E2E SCENARIO INVENTORY. This is critical, because every E2E scenario, success and failure, must still be tested after the migration. For every E2E test function in the repo (in examples/*/tests, lib/e2e tests, benches or anywhere else), give a table row: file path, test function name, contract under test, a one-line description of the scenario, and a classification of SUCCESS (asserts the call succeeds) or FAILURE (asserts a revert or error, and names the expected error or selector if it can). Also state the total count of E2E tests and the total number of success versus failure tests. Look at how lib/e2e/src and lib/e2e-proc/src work: what the #[e2e::test] attribute and the helpers do, how contracts are deployed and activated, and where RPC_URL and DEPLOYER_ADDRESS come from.

6. UNIT TEST INVENTORY. For contracts/, contracts-proc/ and lib/crypto/: the count of #[test] and #[motsu::test] functions per file, and the grand totals. Also doc tests if you can find them.

7. BENCHMARKS. benches/src/*.rs: each benchmarked operation, the contract it targets, and how results are written (benches/src/report.rs). Include the report format.

8. FUZZ TARGETS. fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs and fuzz/src/*: what each target does, its inputs, and its corpus generator.

9. DOCS. docs/modules/ROOT/pages/*.adoc and nav files: each page with its line count, the API names it documents, and any include:: directives or code blocks that reference code paths or API names. Note docs/antora.yml and docs/package.json.

10. CI. For each .github/workflows/*.yml job: the commands it runs, and what it verifies. Keep this short.

11. SCRIPTS. For each scripts/*.sh: what it does and what it needs.

12. TEMPLATES. templates/crypto-erc20: what it is and whether it depends on the library.

13. OPEN QUESTIONS. Anything you could not determine, and anything that looks inconsistent or broken in v0.3.0 (for example a doc that disagrees with the code, a test that is commented out or ignored, #[ignore] markers, TODO or FIXME comments that matter, dead code, or features that are declared but unused). Give file:line for each.

Do NOT assess security findings. Do not read the audit PDFs; another agent will do that.

Work efficiently: use rg or grep with fixed-string patterns and read only what you need. Keep the file under about 250 KB.

WHEN DONE, reply with a summary of at most 20 lines. Include: the file path, the total counts (E2E tests with success and failure split, unit tests, motsu tests, global accessor call sites, examples, docs pages), and the three most important structural observations about composition or about the E2E framework.

   4. Shut the devnet down with `./scripts/nitro-testnode.sh -q` when finished and confirm that no nitro containers remain (`docker ps`).

Be exact, and mark anything not run as NOT RUN.

   Then run the unit tests for the example crates and the benches crate too (`cargo nextest run --locked -p <name>` for each example that has tests), and save their results to /tmp/bench/baseline/example-unit-tests.txt. Note that some examples may only have E2E tests. Report which ones.

B. COVERAGE (CI command, from .github/workflows/test.yml)
   cd /tmp/bench/v030 && cargo llvm-cov --locked -p openzeppelin-stylus -p openzeppelin-stylus-proc -p openzeppelin-crypto --features ruint --summary-only
   Save the summary to /tmp/bench/baseline/coverage-summary.txt. Then produce the per-file line, region and function coverage as JSON with `--json --output-path /tmp/bench/baseline/coverage-v030.json` (same flags). Also save the lcov with --lcov --output-path /tmp/bench/baseline/lcov-v030.info. Report the TOTAL line, region, function and branch percentages (branch coverage only if available on this toolchain; say so if not). Also list the 10 least-covered files with their line coverage. Run coverage in one go with `cargo llvm-cov` and reuse the instrumented build for the JSON/lcov outputs if you can, to save time. Use `cargo llvm-cov clean --workspace` at the start.

C. ABI EXPORT (cargo stylus export-abi, for each example that the CI checks)
   For every directory matching examples/*/ and examples/basic/*/ that has a Cargo.toml with a [package] name (skip the workspace root), run `cargo stylus export-abi` from inside that directory and save stdout to /tmp/bench/baseline/abi/<example-dir-path with / replaced by __>.sol. Also write /tmp/bench/baseline/abi/SUMMARY.txt listing each example and whether export succeeded. For examples/basic/script, note whether it is a binary that does not export an ABI. Report failures verbatim.

D. WASM SIZE AND ACTIVATION CHECK (the CI runs check-wasm.sh, but with -Z build-std; you may build without build-std if it fails and say so)
   Build every example in release mode for wasm32: `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p <crate>` for each example crate (or once with the workspace default-members list if that works). The resulting .wasm files are under /tmp/bench/v030/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/. For each example, run `cargo stylus check --wasm-file <path> -e https://sepolia-rollup.arbitrum.io/rpc` (the Sepolia RPC is reachable and this needs no key). Record the reported compressed contract size and the limit, and whether it passes. Also record the raw .wasm size in bytes and the size after `wasm-opt --enable-bulk-memory -O3` (the same flags as scripts/bench.sh). Save a table to /tmp/bench/baseline/wasm-sizes.md with columns: example, raw bytes, wasm-opt bytes, cargo-stylus compressed size, limit, pass or fail. Pass sleep 2 between cargo stylus calls, as check-wasm.sh does, to avoid rate limits.

E. E2E TESTS AND GAS BENCHMARKS ON THE OLD DEVNET (the v0.3.0 framework)
   This needs the old nitro testnode. Read scripts/nitro-testnode.sh and scripts/e2e-tests.sh and scripts/bench.sh in /tmp/bench/v030 first. The nitro testnode is cloned into /tmp/bench/nitro-testnode (one level above /tmp/bench/v030/scripts, as the script computes). Docker images for it are already present locally (nitro-testnode-rollupcreator, nitro-testnode-scripts, offchainlabs/nitro-node:v3.12.1-70fa99a). If `scripts/nitro-testnode.sh -d -i` fails, capture the error and try to diagnose it. Do not change the script. Report exactly what failed.

Then run `./scripts/bench.sh`. Save the full output to /tmp/bench/baseline/gas-v030.txt. Also copy any generated report file (benches/src/report.rs writes its output somewhere; find it and copy it to /tmp/bench/baseline/). Record the gas numbers per benchmark.
   4. Shut the devnet down with `./scripts/nitro-testnode.sh -q` when finished and confirm that no nitro containers remain (`docker ps`).

1	// Copyright 2024-2025, Offchain Labs, Inc.
     2	// For licensing, see https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/blob/main/licenses/COPYRIGHT.md
     3	
     4	//! Defines host environment methods Stylus SDK contracts have access to.
     5	extern crate alloc;
     6	
     7	use alloc::vec::Vec;
     8	
     9	use alloy_primitives::{Address, B256, U256};
    10	use alloy_sol_types::{abi::token::WordToken, SolEvent, TopicList};
    11	use dyn_clone::DynClone;
    12	
    13	/// The host trait defines methods a Stylus contract can use to interact
    14	/// with a host environment, such as the EVM. It is a composition
    15	/// of traits with different access to host values and modifications.
    16	/// Stylus contracts in the SDK have access to a host via the [`HostAccess`] trait for safe access
    17	/// to hostios without the need for global invocations. The host trait may be implemented
    18	/// by test frameworks as an easier way of mocking hostio invocations for testing
    19	/// Stylus contracts.
    20	pub trait Host:
    21	    CryptographyAccess
    22	    + CalldataAccess
    23	    + UnsafeDeploymentAccess
    24	    + StorageAccess
    25	    + UnsafeCallAccess
    26	    + BlockAccess
    27	    + ChainAccess
    28	    + AccountAccess
    29	    + MemoryAccess
    30	    + MessageAccess
    31	    + MeteringAccess
    32	    + RawLogAccess
    33	    + DynClone
    34	{
    35	}
    36	
    37	// Enables cloning of a boxed, host trait object.
    38	dyn_clone::clone_trait_object!(Host);
    39	
    40	/// Defines a trait that allows a Stylus contract to access its host safely.
    41	pub trait HostAccess {
    42	    /// Host type returned by [`Self::vm()`].
    43	    type Host: Host;
    44	
    45	    /// Provides access to the parametrized host of a contract, giving access
    46	    /// to all the desired hostios from the user.
    47	    fn vm(&self) -> &Self::Host;
    48	}
    49	
    50	/// Defines a trait that can deny access to a contract router method if a message value is
    51	/// passed in while the method is non-payable.
    52	pub trait ValueDenier {
    53	    fn deny_value(&self, method_name: &str) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
    54	}
    55	
    56	/// Defines a trait that guards whether the constructor was already called.
    57	pub trait ConstructorGuard {
    58	    fn check_constructor_slot(&self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;

#!/bin/bash

MYDIR=$(realpath "$(dirname "$0")")
cd "$MYDIR" || exit

HAS_INIT=false
HAS_DETACH=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
  -i | --init)
    HAS_INIT=true
    shift
    ;;
  -d | --detach)
    HAS_DETACH=true
    shift
    ;;
  -q | --quit)
    NITRO_CONTAINERS=$(docker container ls -q --filter name=nitro-testnode)

    if [ -z "$NITRO_CONTAINERS" ]; then
      echo "No nitro-testnode containers running"
    else
      docker container stop $NITRO_CONTAINERS || exit
    fi

    exit 0
    ;;
  *)
    echo "OPTIONS:"
    echo "-i|--init:         clone repo and init nitro test node"
    echo "-d|--detach:       setup nitro test node in detached mode"
    echo "-q|--quit:         shutdown nitro test node docker containers"
    exit 0
    ;;
  esac
done

TEST_NODE_DIR="$MYDIR/../nitro-testnode"
if [ ! -d "$TEST_NODE_DIR" ]; then
  HAS_INIT=true
fi

if $HAS_INIT; then
  cd "$MYDIR" || exit
  cd ..

  git clone -b release --recurse-submodules https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro-testnode.git
  cd ./nitro-testnode || exit
  git checkout c7a58620c431266c90f9d422eca6627e24586e60 || exit

  ./test-node.bash --no-run --init || exit
fi

cd "$TEST_NODE_DIR" || exit
if $HAS_DETACH; then
  ./test-node.bash --detach
else
  ./test-node.bash
fi

#!/bin/bash
set -e

MYDIR=$(realpath "$(dirname "$0")")
cd "$MYDIR"
cd ..

# Optimize contract's wasm binary by crate name.
opt_wasm() {
  local CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME=$1
  local CONTRACT_BIN_NAME="${CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME//-/_}.wasm"
  local CONTRACT_OPT_BIN_NAME="${CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME//-/_}_opt.wasm"

  echo
  echo "Optimizing $CONTRACT_CRATE_NAME WASM binary"
  # https://rustwasm.github.io/book/reference/code-size.html#use-the-wasm-opt-tool
  wasm-opt --enable-bulk-memory -O3 -o ./target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/"$CONTRACT_OPT_BIN_NAME" ./target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/"$CONTRACT_BIN_NAME"
}

# Retrieve all alphanumeric contract's crate names in `./examples` directory.
get_example_crate_names() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC2038
  # NOTE: optimistically relying on the 'name = ' string at Cargo.toml file
  find ./examples -maxdepth 2 -type f -name "Cargo.toml" | xargs grep 'name = ' | grep -oE '".*"' | tr -d "'\""
}

cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
  -Z build-std=std,panic_abort \
  -Z build-std-features=panic_immediate_abort

# Optimize contract's wasm for gas usage.
for CRATE_NAME in $(get_example_crate_names); do
  opt_wasm "$CRATE_NAME"
done

export RPC_URL=http://localhost:8547
export DEPLOYER_ADDRESS=0xcEcba2F1DC234f70Dd89F2041029807F8D03A990

# No need to compile benchmarks with `--release`
# since this only runs the benchmarking code and the contracts have already been compiled with `--release`.
cargo run -p benches
echo "This benchmarks measure gas execution cost,
 the 21000 EVM base gas fee is omitted."
echo
echo "To measure non cached contract's gas usage correctly,
 benchmarks should run on a clean instance of the nitro test node."
echo
echo "Finished running benches!"

#!/bin/bash
# Logging wrapper used for the v0.3.0 baseline run.
# Usage: rl.sh <working-dir> <command-string>
# Appends the start time, working directory, command and exit status to
# /tmp/bench/baseline/commands.log, then runs the command under bash with pipefail.
LOG=/tmp/bench/baseline/commands.log
cwd="$1"
shift
cmd="$*"
{
  echo "=== $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) cwd=${cwd}"
  echo "+ ${cmd}"
} >> "$LOG"
if ! cd "$cwd"; then
  echo "    exit=127 (cannot cd to ${cwd})" >> "$LOG"
  exit 127
fi
bash -o pipefail -c "$cmd"
rc=$?
echo "    exit=${rc} end=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$LOG"
exit $rc

# Design observations on v0.3.0 (working notes, not a deliverable)

Source: /tmp/bench/v030 (tag v0.3.0). Read directly by the lead agent.

## Composition in the reference example (examples/erc20/src/lib.rs)

- `Erc20Example` is a `#[entrypoint] #[storage]` struct with four composed fields:
  `erc20: Erc20`, `metadata: Erc20Metadata`, `capped: Capped`, `pausable: Pausable`.
- Every extension trait the consumer exposes is re-implemented by hand in the
  example as a `#[public] impl I... for Erc20Example`, and each method is a
  one-line delegation (`self.erc20.total_supply()`, `self.metadata.name()`, ...).
  This is boilerplate every consumer repeats, and the example is ~250 lines for
  an ERC-20 with three extensions.
- The top-level error is a hand-written enum that flattens the sub-errors
  (`ExceededCap`, `InvalidCap`, `InsufficientBalance`, ...). Each sub-error needs
  a `From<sub::Error> for Error` impl written by hand: ~40 lines of pure mapping.
- `#[implements(IErc20<Error = Error>, IErc20Burnable<Error = Error>, ...)]` must
  list every interface by hand; a missing entry is a silent ABI gap.
- `supports_interface` is hand-written and must OR together the interface IDs of
  every composed component.

## Safety footgun: pause and cap checks are per-call-site

- `Pausable::when_not_paused()` is called manually in `transfer`, `transfer_from`,
  `burn`, `burn_from` and `mint` of the example. Any new entry point that forgets
  the check silently bypasses the pause. This is the same class of bug Solidity
  avoids by overriding `_update`, which all balance changes route through.
- Cap enforcement is also per-call-site: the example's comment says "You should
  not call `Erc20::_update` to mint tokens -- it will break `Capped`", which means
  correctness depends on a comment, not on the type system.
- Target design (to be validated against SDK 0.10.10 capabilities): one
  balance-update path that every mint, burn and transfer goes through, with
  extensions hooking into it, so that pause and cap apply by construction.

## Proc macro surface

- `contracts-proc` provides a single attribute: `#[interface_id]`. It XORs the
  selectors of a trait into the ERC-165 ID and rejects duplicate Solidity
  signatures at compile time (`compile_fail` doc test). Keep this behaviour.

## Release profile (root Cargo.toml)

- `[profile.release]`: `opt-level = "z"`, `lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1`,
  `panic = "abort"`, `strip = true`. Size-oriented already.
- `[profile.dev] panic = "abort"`.
- CI size check uses `-Z build-std=std,panic_abort` with
  `panic_immediate_abort`, which stable 1.91.0 cannot do. Expect WASM size to rise
  on stable; measure before deciding anything (baseline agent is measuring).

## Size of the code in scope (lines of .rs, including tests)

- contracts 28,254; contracts-proc 218; lib/crypto 13,214; lib/e2e 1,018;
  lib/e2e-proc 68; benches 1,865; fuzz 274.

## Things to check against the agents' reports before design is final

- SDK 0.10.10: does `#[inherit]`/`#[borrow]` give method delegation and override
  semantics that remove the hand-written delegation? Can the host (`self.vm()`)
  be reached from storage helpers? Is there a hook point for `_update`-style
  checks?
- stylus-test: how many lines of motsu-style setup per test will remain?
- stylus-tools devnet: does it give us a provider and deploy helpers that shrink
  the per-example E2E files?

2	# Logging wrapper used for the v0.3.0 baseline run.
3	# Usage: rl.sh <working-dir> <command-string>
4	# Appends the start time, working directory, command and exit status to
5	# /tmp/bench/baseline/commands.log, then runs the command under bash with pipefail.
6	LOG=/tmp/bench/baseline/commands.log
7	cwd="$1"
8	shift
9	cmd="$*"
10	{
11	  echo "=== $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) cwd=${cwd}"
12	  echo "+ ${cmd}"
13	} >> "$LOG"
14	if ! cd "$cwd"; then
15	  echo "    exit=127 (cannot cd to ${cwd})" >> "$LOG"
16	  exit 127
17	fi
18	bash -o pipefail -c "$cmd"
19	rc=$?
20	echo "    exit=${rc} end=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$LOG"
21	exit $rc

#!/bin/bash
# Logging wrapper used for the v0.3.0 baseline run.
# Usage: rl.sh <working-dir> <command-string>
# Runs the command under bash with pipefail (stdout/stderr go to the caller). After it
# finishes, appends ONE entry to /tmp/bench/baseline/commands.log with the start/end
# time, working directory, command text and exit status.
LOG=/tmp/bench/baseline/commands.log
cwd="$1"
shift
cmd="$*"
start=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
if ! cd "$cwd" 2>/dev/null; then
  printf '[%s] cwd=%s\n  $ %s\n  exit=127 (cannot cd)\n' "$start" "$cwd" "$cmd" >> "$LOG"
  exit 127
fi
bash -o pipefail -c "$cmd"
rc=$?
end=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
printf '[%s..%s] cwd=%s\n  $ %s\n  exit=%s\n' "$start" "$end" "$cwd" "$cmd" "$rc" >> "$LOG"
exit $rc

You are classifying end-to-end (E2E) tests in a read-only snapshot. Repo root: /tmp/bench/v030 (OpenZeppelin Stylus contracts library, tag v0.3.0). Use absolute paths.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Read-only analysis. Do NOT modify anything under /tmp/bench/v030 or /private/tmp/bench/ws. Do NOT run cargo, rustc, npm, or install anything. Do NOT read any PDF.
- You may write exactly ONE file: the output TSV path given at the end. Create no other files.

FRAMEWORK FACTS (verified from source)
- `#[e2e::test]` (lib/e2e-proc/src/test.rs) rewrites `async fn t(alice: Account, bob: Account) -> Result<()>` into a `#[tokio::test]`, creating each parameter with `Account::new().await?`. Accounts are funded by a nitro test node (lib/e2e/src/account.rs).
- `alice.as_deployer().with_constructor(c).deploy().await?.contract_address` (lib/e2e/src/deploy.rs) runs `cargo stylus deploy --no-verify` on the wasm of the crate's #[entrypoint], which deploys and activates it via StylusDeployer. `.with_example_name("x")` deploys the wasm named `x_example`.
- lib/e2e/src/lib.rs: `send!(e)` = `e.send().await` (returns Err if the node rejects the tx, e.g. at gas estimation with a revert). `receipt!(e)` = `send!(e)?.get_receipt().await`. `watch!(e)` = `send!(e)?.watch().await`.
- lib/e2e/src/event.rs: `receipt.emits(Event { .. })` checks the receipt logs for an event.
- lib/e2e/src/error.rs: `err.reverted_with(ErrType { .. })` checks the revert data of an alloy contract error or an eyre report. `err.panicked_with(PanicCode::X)` checks only code -32000 and message "execution reverted"; the PanicCode argument is IGNORED by the framework.
- Some tests live inside `mod name { ... }` blocks; the test name in the list includes the module path, e.g. `constructor::success`.

CLASSIFICATION RULES (apply exactly)
- FAILURE: the test asserts that a call or transaction fails. Look for `expect_err`, `unwrap_err`, `.is_err()`, `reverted_with(`, `panicked_with(`, `matches!(.., Err(..))`, or any other explicit error assertion on the call under test. Successful setup transactions before the asserted failure do not change this: still FAILURE.
- FAILURE (no revert): if the test asserts that a call returns `false` (or another unsuccessful return value) without reverting, classify FAILURE and write `return false (no revert)` in the expected column.
- SUCCESS: every asserted call succeeds; the test only asserts state, balances, return values other than false, or emitted events; it has no error or false-return assertion.
- If you cannot tell, read more: helpers in the same file, tests/mock/*.rs, tests/abi/mod.rs (ABI and error definitions). Do not guess silently; report unsure cases.

OUTPUT
Write the TSV to the output path given below. UTF-8, LF newlines, one header line, then one row per listed test in list order, 7 tab-separated columns, no embedded tabs or newlines:
file<TAB>line<TAB>test<TAB>contract_under_test<TAB>description<TAB>class<TAB>expected
- file: repo-relative path, e.g. examples/erc20/tests/erc20.rs
- line: the line number from the list
- test: module path plus function name, exactly as in the list (e.g. constructor::success)
- contract_under_test: the Rust contract type or example name whose behavior the test targets (e.g. Erc20, Erc721Wrapper, mock Erc20 with failing transfer). Short name.
- description: one line, at most 160 characters: what is called with which inputs, and what is asserted (e.g. "mint to Address::ZERO; expects revert and unchanged balance and totalSupply").
- class: SUCCESS or FAILURE
- expected: for FAILURE, the error type as written in the test (e.g. Erc20::ERC20InvalidReceiver), or the panic code, or the selector, or `return false (no revert)`. For SUCCESS, `-`.

COVERAGE
/tmp/bench/notes/e2e-parts/list.tsv has every E2E test (columns: file, line, test), extracted mechanically from the source. Filter it for your files. Produce exactly one row per listed test for your files: no missing rows, no extra rows, no helper functions.

FINAL REPLY (under 15 lines): output path, data row count, SUCCESS count, FAILURE count, count of `return false (no revert)` rows, and the test names where you were unsure, with the reason. Do not paste the table into the reply.

You are classifying end-to-end (E2E) tests in a read-only snapshot. Repo root: /tmp/bench/v030 (OpenZeppelin Stylus contracts library, tag v0.3.0). Use absolute paths.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Read-only analysis. Do NOT modify anything under /tmp/bench/v030 or /private/tmp/bench/ws. Do NOT run cargo, rustc, npm, or install anything. Do NOT read any PDF.
- You may write exactly ONE file: the output TSV path given at the end. Create no other files.

FRAMEWORK FACTS (verified from source)
- `#[e2e::test]` (lib/e2e-proc/src/test.rs) rewrites `async fn t(alice: Account, bob: Account) -> Result<()>` into a `#[tokio::test]`, creating each parameter with `Account::new().await?`. Accounts are funded by a nitro test node (lib/e2e/src/account.rs).
- `alice.as_deployer().with_constructor(c).deploy().await?.contract_address` (lib/e2e/src/deploy.rs) runs `cargo stylus deploy --no-verify` on the wasm of the crate's #[entrypoint], which deploys and activates it via StylusDeployer. `.with_example_name("x")` deploys the wasm named `x_example`.
- lib/e2e/src/lib.rs: `send!(e)` = `e.send().await` (returns Err if the node rejects the tx, e.g. at gas estimation with a revert). `receipt!(e)` = `send!(e)?.get_receipt().await`. `watch!(e)` = `send!(e)?.watch().await`.
- lib/e2e/src/event.rs: `receipt.emits(Event { .. })` checks the receipt logs for an event.
- lib/e2e/src/error.rs: `err.reverted_with(ErrType { .. })` checks the revert data of an alloy contract error or an eyre report. `err.panicked_with(PanicCode::X)` checks only code -32000 and message "execution reverted"; the PanicCode argument is IGNORED by the framework.
- Some tests live inside `mod name { ... }` blocks; the test name in the list includes the module path, e.g. `constructor::success`.

CLASSIFICATION RULES (apply exactly)
- FAILURE: the test asserts that a call or transaction fails. Look for `expect_err`, `unwrap_err`, `.is_err()`, `reverted_with(`, `panicked_with(`, `matches!(.., Err(..))`, or any other explicit error assertion on the call under test. Successful setup transactions before the asserted failure do not change this: still FAILURE.
- FAILURE (no revert): if the test asserts that a call returns `false` (or another unsuccessful return value) without reverting, classify FAILURE and write `return false (no revert)` in the expected column.
- SUCCESS: every asserted call succeeds; the test only asserts state, balances, return values other than false, or emitted events; it has no error or false-return assertion.
- If you cannot tell, read more: helpers in the same file, tests/mock/*.rs, tests/abi/mod.rs (ABI and error definitions). Do not guess silently; report unsure cases.

OUTPUT
Write the TSV to the output path given below. UTF-8, LF newlines, one header line, then one row per listed test in list order, 7 tab-separated columns, no embedded tabs or newlines:
file<TAB>line<TAB>test<TAB>contract_under_test<TAB>description<TAB>class<TAB>expected
- file: repo-relative path, e.g. examples/erc20/tests/erc20.rs
- line: the line number from the list
- test: module path plus function name, exactly as in the list (e.g. constructor::success)
- contract_under_test: the Rust contract type or example name whose behavior the test targets (e.g. Erc20, Erc721Wrapper, mock Erc20 with failing transfer). Short name.
- description: one line, at most 160 characters: what is called with which inputs, and what is asserted (e.g. "mint to Address::ZERO; expects revert and unchanged balance and totalSupply").
- class: SUCCESS or FAILURE
- expected: for FAILURE, the error type as written in the test (e.g. Erc20::ERC20InvalidReceiver), or the panic code, or the selector, or `return false (no revert)`. For SUCCESS, `-`.

COVERAGE
/tmp/bench/notes/e2e-parts/list.tsv has every E2E test (columns: file, line, test), extracted mechanically from the source. Filter it for your files. Produce exactly one row per listed test for your files: no missing rows, no extra rows, no helper functions.

FINAL REPLY (under 15 lines): output path, data row count, SUCCESS count, FAILURE count, count of `return false (no revert)` rows, and the test names where you were unsure, with the reason. Do not paste the table into the reply.

## b. Methodology, limitations and exclusions

- Methodology: not stated. The report has no methodology section. Its sections are Summary, Scope, System Overview, Security Model and Trust Assumptions, findings, Recommendations, Conclusion.
- Limitations section: none. The report has no list of stated limitations.
- Trust assumptions and security model (p.9, "Security Model and Trust Assumptions"), copied as printed:
  - "The crypto library's Poseidon2 implementation matches the test vectors of the reference implementation."
  - "It is assumed that the Stylus SDK and all third-party dependencies used by the Contracts for Stylus library are secure, free from malicious code (such as backdoors), and behave as documented."
  - "Motsu, OpenZeppelin's internal testing utility for Stylus contracts, functions as intended, contains no critical bugs, and provides reliable coverage for the library's unit tests."
- Out of scope: the report has no explicit out-of-scope list. The scope is the two parts listed above. The pedersen directory is in scope and was added by commit 2350766.

## c. Findings: severity-rated (High, Medium, Low)

Informational findings (section "Notes & Additional Information") are in section e. The M-02 title is printed with "Customer" (not "Custom") and is transcribed as printed.

| ID | Title | Severity (as printed) | Status | Affected file / function | Description (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H-01 | Limb Shift Overflow in shr_assign and shl_assign | High Severity | Resolved | shr_assign and shl_assign (Uint<N> shift-and-assign operators) | Shifting with a limb_shift of zero overflows, which panics in debug builds and masks the shift amount in release builds, producing wrong results. |
| M-01 | Potential Underflow in ct_rem Function | Medium Severity | Resolved | ct_rem (index calculation) | The index calculation underflows when the dividend is zero, because ct_num_bits() returns zero, and the value wraps in release mode. |
| M-02 | Customer Selectors in Trait With interface_id Attribute Are Not Checked in Implementation | Medium Severity | Acknowledged | interface_id procedural macro; #[selector] in traits | Custom selectors declared in a trait marked with #[interface_id] are not checked against trait implementations, so an implementation's ABI can differ from its trait. |
| L-01 | Verification Functions for Custom Hashing in Merkle Trees Assume Commutative Hashing | Low Severity | Resolved | verify_with_builder, verify_multi_proof_with_builder | The Merkle verifiers with custom hashing assume the custom hash is commutative, which cannot be guaranteed. |
| L-02 | Inconsistent Data Types for carry and borrow Parameters | Low Severity | Resolved | adc, sbb (Limb type) vs adc_assign, sbb_assign (bool type) | carry and borrow are typed Limb in adc and sbb but bool in adc_assign and sbb_assign, so a value above 1 can break overflow protection. |
| L-03 | Encoding Ambiguity in ct_num_bits Function | Low Severity | Resolved | ct_num_bits | ct_num_bits returns 0 for the number 0, though at least one bit is needed to encode any value. |
| L-04 | Absence of Overflow Check in from_str_hex Function | Low Severity | Resolved | from_str_hex | from_str_hex does not check for overflow when parsing into Uint<LIMBS>, unlike from_str_radix, which uses an overflow check in ct_add. |
| L-05 | Underlying Decimals in Erc20Wrapper Can Be Set Incorrectly | Low Severity | Resolved | Erc20Wrapper constructor; underlying_decimals | The constructor sets the underlying token address but not underlying_decimals, which must be set by hand. |
| L-06 | State Mutability Can Be Restricted in IErc4626 | Low Severity | Resolved | IErc4626 trait: total_assets, convert_to_shares, convert_to_assets, etc. | Read-only IErc4626 methods take &mut self, which lets an implementation change state inside a read-only function. |
| L-07 | Custom Selectors in Trait With interface_id Allows Unreachable Patterns | Low Severity | Resolved | Traits with #[interface_id] and #[selector] | Traits can declare duplicate selectors that can never be implemented, unlike #[public] blocks, which raise an unreachable pattern error. |
| L-08 | Missing Trait Components in Generated Code From interface_id Macro | Low Severity | Resolved | interface_id macro (ty_generics; unsafe qualifier) | The regenerated trait drops generic bounds and the unsafe qualifier. |
| L-09 | Potential Vulnerability in Big Integer Library to Timing Side-Channel Attacks | Low Severity | Resolved | ct_ge(), ct_gt(), cmp() (big integer library) | These comparison functions return early, so execution time can depend on the input values. |

| M-01 | Resolved | Update: Resolved in pull #667 at commit 36ab98e. | #667 | 36ab98e |

The Contracts for Stylus team stated: [blockquote] "We have recommended the Stylus SDK team to include the #[interface_id] functionality and the option to retrieve selectors of each method and auto-implement each router function to build inheritance this way (Doing so would allow compile-time checks on custom selector differences between traits and implementation). ## e. Informational / notes findings

The report's section heading is "Notes & Additional Information". It has no separate gas or informational label.

| ID | Title | Severity (as printed) | Status | Affected file / function | Description (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| N-01 | Consistent Application of the #[must_use] Attribute in Merkle Proof Verification Functions | Notes & Additional Information | Resolved | Merkle module: verify, verify_multi_proof | verify carries #[must_use] but verify_multi_proof does not, so the attribute is applied inconsistently. |
| N-02 | Redundant Attribute in the adc Function | Notes & Additional Information | Resolved | adc function | The function-level #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)] is redundant with a file-level attribute. |
| N-03 | Absence of #[inline(always)] Attributes in Certain Methods | Notes & Additional Information | Resolved | Uint methods ct_lt, ct_is_zero, ct_eq | These methods lack #[inline(always)], while similar methods ct_ge, ct_gt and ct_le have it. |
| N-04 | Incorrect Comment in PartialEq Implementation for Projective Points | Notes & Additional Information | Resolved | PartialEq for Projective (sw curve) | The comment gives the cross-multiplied equality conditions in a different form from the one the code checks. |
| N-05 | Source Code Attribution Concerns | Notes & Additional Information | Resolved | curve module (code from algebra/ec); field module (code from algebra/ff) | Code taken from external codebases is not attributed in the comments. |
| N-06 | Documentation Enhancements | Notes & Additional Information | Resolved | absorb and squeeze functions; Poseidon2 interface | The report asks for comments on the one-way absorb to squeeze transition and for a statement that padding and domain separation are the user's responsibility. |
| N-07 | Inconsistent Behavior of Shift Overflow Compared to Rust Native Integer Types | Notes & Additional Information | Resolved | shr_assign, shl_assign | Shift overflow returns Zero here, while Rust native integers mask the shift amount. |
| N-08 | Misleading Documentation | Notes & Additional Information | Resolved partially | #[interface_id] macro documentation | The docs say the macro adds an associated constant, but it adds a function. |
| N-09 | Typographical Errors | Notes & Additional Information | Resolved | underline_token variable; test prevents_non_onwers_from_transferring; comment at line 111 of contracts/src/access/control.rs | Several typos in identifiers, a test name and a comment. |
| N-10 | Insufficient Unit Test Coverage | Notes & Additional Information | Acknowledged | crypto arithmetic limb.rs | Some code, such as limb.rs, lacks unit tests that exercise all of its functions. |

## f. Out of scope, open items, and other stated caveats

- Explicit out-of-scope list: none in the report.
- Acknowledged and left open by the report: M-02 ("Acknowledged, will resolve."), N-10 ("Acknowledged, will resolve."). Their resolution text is in section d.
- Partially resolved: N-08 (printed as "Resolved partially"). Its resolution text is in section d.
- Recommendations (p.19, "Recommendations" section; these are not numbered findings), copied as printed:
  - "Check for Poseidon2 S-box Invertibility: Add a check gcd(P::D, F::MODULUS - 1) == 1 in the new() function to ensure the invertibility of the S-box mapping f(x)=x^D."
  - "Enforce Even Number of Full Rounds and Minimal Number of Rounds in Poseidon2: According to the Poseidon2 paper, the total number of full rounds must be an even number. The current implementation assumes this condition is met. Consider adding a check to ensure that this requirement is enforced. Also, a minimal number of rounds must be done to achieve the required security parameter."
- Conclusion (p.20): "The audit identified one high-severity issue and two medium-severity issues, along with several low-severity findings and general notes across the contracts and crypto library scopes." It also says "regular audits are strongly recommended whenever major library updates are introduced."
- Trust assumptions (p.9): quoted in section b.

content.content:
Stylus Contracts Library v0.3.0 Audit − Summary − 3
 Scope
OpenZeppelin audited the OpenZeppelin/rust-contracts-stylus library at commit 231d4f1
( v0.3.0-rc.1 ). This is a follow-up audit after the v0.2.0 audit, focusing on the refactors and
newly added features.

In scope are all the changes made in the following directories:

├── contracts/**/*.rs
├── contracts-proc/src/**/*.rs
└── lib/crypto/src/**/*.rs


The pull requests containing the in-scope changes are listed here.




--- trust ---

Security Model and Trust
Assumptions
This audit assumes that the Stylus SDK and all third-party dependencies used by the audited
library are secure and behave as documented. Users of the audited library are assumed to



 Stylus Contracts Library v0.3.0 Audit − System Overview − 5
 strictly follow the API descriptions, warnings, and examples to avoid potential errors.
Especially, the following assumptions apply:

 • Users of the UUPS proxy will adhere to the upgrade guidelines, properly initializing the
 proxy and incrementing the version number in new implementations.
 • The signing functions of Ed25519 signatures should only be used in an off-chain
 environment, with the ExpandedSecretKey data kept confidential.




 Stylus Contracts Library v0.3.0 Audit − Security Model and Trust
 Assumptions − 6
 High Severity
--- L-04 blockquote + update ---
Existent Tokens or Contracts with Fallbacks
The allowance function is called by safe_increase_allowance and
safe_decrease_allowance to read the current allowance of the spender . In pull request
#765, the Address::has_code(&token) check in allowance was removed with a
comment:

 There's no code check in Solidity. In case of no code, a 0 (zero) is expected as the
 result

 For reference, the Solidity code is token.allowance(address(this),
 spender) .

However, the Solidity compiler performs an existence check before making any high-level calls,
and reverts if the check fails. Such calls also revert if the return data cannot be decoded as
uint256 . By contrast, the Stylus implementation decodes empty return data as zero via
U256::from_be_slice(&result) . This creates two inconsistencies with the Solidity
library:

 • When token is set to a non-existent address, the Solidity call reverts, while Stylus
 returns 0 .
 • When token is set to a non-ERC-20 contract that has a fallback function, the Solidity
 call reverts, while Stylus returns 0 .

Consider updating allowance to first check whether token exists and requires exactly 32
bytes of return data ( U256 ).

Update: Resolved in pull #833 and merged at commit 0015161. The team added a check to
ensure the token contract exists and replaced the RawCall with a high-level call.

#!/bin/bash
# A4: run `cargo nextest run --locked -p <name>` for every example crate (examples/*/ and
# examples/basic/*/ with a [package] name) and for the benches crate.
# Every cargo call goes through rl.sh so it is recorded in commands.log with its exit status.
RL=/tmp/bench/baseline/tools/rl.sh
SRC=/tmp/bench/v030
OUTDIR=/tmp/bench/baseline/example-tests
OUT=/tmp/bench/baseline/example-unit-tests.txt
mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"
: > "$OUT"

names=$(cd "$SRC" && for f in examples/*/Cargo.toml examples/basic/*/Cargo.toml benches/Cargo.toml; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && grep -m1 '^name = ' "$f" | sed -E 's/^name = "(.*)"/\1/'
done)

for p in $names; do
  log="$OUTDIR/$p.txt"
  CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 "$RL" "$SRC" "cargo nextest run --locked -p $p > $log 2>&1"
  rc=$?
  {
    echo "##### cargo nextest run --locked -p $p  (exit=$rc)"
    cat "$log"
    echo
  } >> "$OUT"
  echo "$p exit=$rc"
done
echo "ALL DONE"

11	  one-line delegation (`self.erc20.total_supply()`, `self.metadata.name()`, ...).
12	  This is boilerplate every consumer repeats, and the example is ~250 lines for
13	  an ERC-20 with three extensions.
14	- The top-level error is a hand-written enum that flattens the sub-errors
15	  (`ExceededCap`, `InvalidCap`, `InsufficientBalance`, ...). Each sub-error needs
16	  a `From<sub::Error> for Error` impl written by hand: ~40 lines of pure mapping.
17	- `#[implements(IErc20<Error = Error>, IErc20Burnable<Error = Error>, ...)]` must
18	  list every interface by hand; a missing entry is a silent ABI gap.
19	- `supports_interface` is hand-written and must OR together the interface IDs of
20	  every composed component.
21	
22	## Safety footgun: pause and cap checks are per-call-site
23	
24	- `Pausable::when_not_paused()` is called manually in `transfer`, `transfer_from`,
25	  `burn`, `burn_from` and `mint` of the example. Any new entry point that forgets
26	  the check silently bypasses the pause. This is the same class of bug Solidity
27	  avoids by overriding `_update`, which all balance changes route through.
28	- Cap enforcement is also per-call-site: the example's comment says "You should
29	  not call `Erc20::_update` to mint tokens -- it will break `Capped`", which means
30	  correctness depends on a comment, not on the type system.
31	- Target design (to be validated against SDK 0.10.10 capabilities): one
32	  balance-update path that every mint, burn and transfer goes through, with
33	  extensions hooking into it, so that pause and cap apply by construction.
34	
35	## Proc macro surface
36	
37	- `contracts-proc` provides a single attribute: `#[interface_id]`. It XORs the
38	  selectors of a trait into the ERC-165 ID and rejects duplicate Solidity
39	  signatures at compile time (`compile_fail` doc test). Keep this behaviour.
40	
41	## Release profile (root Cargo.toml)
42	
43	- `[profile.release]`: `opt-level = "z"`, `lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1`,
44	  `panic = "abort"`, `strip = true`. Size-oriented already.
45	- `[profile.dev] panic = "abort"`.
46	- CI size check uses `-Z build-std=std,panic_abort` with
47	  `panic_immediate_abort`, which stable 1.91.0 cannot do. Expect WASM size to rise
48	  on stable; measure before deciding anything (baseline agent is measuring).
49	
50	## Size of the code in scope (lines of .rs, including tests)
51	
52	- contracts 28,254; contracts-proc 218; lib/crypto 13,214; lib/e2e 1,018;
53	  lib/e2e-proc 68; benches 1,865; fuzz 274.
54	
55	## Things to check against the agents' reports before design is final
56	
57	- SDK 0.10.10: does `#[inherit]`/`#[borrow]` give method delegation and override
58	  semantics that remove the hand-written delegation? Can the host (`self.vm()`)
59	  be reached from storage helpers? Is there a hook point for `_update`-style
60	  checks?
61	- stylus-test: how many lines of motsu-style setup per test will remain?
62	- stylus-tools devnet: does it give us a provider and deploy helpers that shrink
63	  the per-example E2E files?

#!/bin/bash
# C: `cargo stylus export-abi` in every example crate directory (examples/*/ and
# examples/basic/*/ that have a Cargo.toml with a [package] section). stdout goes to
# abi/<dir with / replaced by __>.sol, stderr to abi/logs/, and SUMMARY.txt gets one line per crate.
RL=/tmp/bench/baseline/tools/rl.sh
SRC=/tmp/bench/v030
OUT=/tmp/bench/baseline/abi
mkdir -p "$OUT/logs"
SUMMARY="$OUT/SUMMARY.txt"
: > "$SUMMARY"

dirs=$(cd "$SRC" && for d in examples/*/ examples/basic/*/; do
  d=${d%/}
  [ -f "$d/Cargo.toml" ] && grep -q '^\[package\]' "$d/Cargo.toml" && echo "$d"
done)

for d in $dirs; do
  name=$(echo "$d" | sed 's#/#__#g')
  CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 "$RL" "$SRC/$d" "cargo stylus export-abi > $OUT/$name.sol 2> $OUT/logs/$name.stderr.txt"
  rc=$?
  bytes=$(wc -c < "$OUT/$name.sol" | tr -d ' ')
  if [ "$rc" = 0 ]; then status=OK; else status=FAILED; fi
  echo "$d | $status | exit=$rc | stdout_bytes=$bytes | $name.sol" >> "$SUMMARY"
  echo "$d $status exit=$rc"
done
echo "ABI DONE"

# Changelog

These crates follow [semver](https://semver.org).

## [0.10.10](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.10) - 2026-10-02

### New

- Detect when Stylus activations are paused on the target chain and report a clear `ActivationsPaused` error instead of a generic activation failure [#458](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/458)

### Fixed

- Support `ruint >=1.17.1` and drop the vulnerable exact pin [#457](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/457)

## [0.10.9](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.9) - 2026-08-11

### New

- Add opt-in reproducible `wasm-opt` (Binaryen) optimization: a `[wasm-opt]` table in `Stylus.toml` pins a Binaryen version and flags, applied identically during deploy and verification and folded into the project hash [#449](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/449)

## [0.10.8](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.8) - 2026-07-06

### Fixed

- Fix `cargo stylus verify` for fragmented (large) contracts whose init code is split across multiple deployment transactions [#445](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/445)

## [0.10.7](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.7) - 2026-05-19

### Fixed

- Fix `cargo stylus verify` not forwarding `--endpoint` and `--skip-clean` flags to inner Docker invocation

## [0.10.6](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.6) - 2026-05-15

### New

- Add Dockerfile for building `cargo-stylus-base` Docker image from the monorepo
- Add reproducible Docker build path to `cargo stylus deploy` — previously deploy always built locally even when `--no-verify` was omitted, making Docker verification unreliable on cross-platform setups

### Fixed

- Fix reproducible Docker builds for workspace projects: mount workspace root instead of CWD so workspace-level `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and path dependencies are available inside the container
- Fix `cargo stylus verify` not forwarding `--contract` flag to inner Docker invocation, causing incorrect contract selection in multi-contract workspaces
- Fix reproducible build failing when base Docker image exists locally but not on Docker Hub

## [0.10.5](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.5) - 2026-04-16

### Changed

- Deprecate `reentrant` feature flag and `deny_reentrant` entrypoint guard — reentrancy safety is provided by automatic storage cache flushing in high-level call functions, making the guard redundant
- Rewrite reentrancy documentation to center cache flushing as the primary safety mechanism

## [0.10.4](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.4) - 2026-04-09

### Fixed

- Fix `cargo stylus new` panic when installed from crates.io registry [#421](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/421)

## [0.10.3](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.3) - 2026-04-01

### New

- Detect ABI selector collisions at compile time within `#[public]` blocks [#401](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/401)

### Fixed

- Fix `sol_interface!` ABI decode panic on multi-value return types containing dynamic types (e.g. `returns (string, uint256)`) [#414](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/414)
- Fix `cargo stylus new` leaving projects in a broken state when dependency resolution fails [#416](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/416)
- Fix codehash-keepalive command sending read-only call instead of transaction [#411](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/411)

### Changed

- Update Rust toolchain to 1.91.0 and alloy dependencies to latest (alloy-primitives/alloy-sol-types 1.5.7, alloy 1.7.3) [#410](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/410)
- Update MSRV to 1.91.0 [#410](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/410)
- Remove exact version pins on `ruint`, `branches`, and `rclite`; disable `ruint` default features to prevent `std` leaking into WASM builds [#413](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/413)
- Switch ABI decoding to validating variants that reject malformed data [#415](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/415)
- Adopt stricter `rustfmt` configuration [#417](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/417)
- Extensive integration test improvements for examples [#365](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/365)
- Improve smoke test for `cargo stylus new` with scaffolding verification [#416](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/416)

## [0.10.2](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.2) - 2026-03-09

### Fixed

- Pin `keccak` dependency to `>=0.1.6` to avoid resolving to broken `0.1.5` [#397](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/pull/397)

## [0.10.0](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.10.0)

### New

- Introduction of a new library for building and deploying stylus contracts: `stylus-tools`
- Support for cargo workspaces. Cargo-stylus now supports building and deploying contracts within a cargo workspace. Contracts are marked with a `Stylus.toml` file. Future configuration will be added to this file to facilitate per-contract and workspace-wide configuration options for contracts.
- Addition of a new `contract-client-gen` feature flag which allows contracts within a crate to be used as a "library" to be called by other contracts.
- Support for nested structs in return types
- More convenient integer functions for storage
- Support for custom storage slots
- Support for tuples in return types
- cargo stylus codehash-keepalive command

### Changed

- Update calls / deploys / logs to use noew hostio model
- Additional integration tests
- Upgrade alloy version
- More example contracts from Stylus By Example
- Use alloy::Bytes type instead of our own
- Improvements to CI
- Move `cargo-stylus` into the `OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs` repo to simplify development and release of new cargo-stylus versions
- Updates to `cargo stylus new` for creating workspaces and individual contracts (`--workspace` and `--contract` flags respectively)
- Allow pure functions in trait-based inheritance model
- Traits used for contract routing inheritance must now use the `#[public]` macro
- Mini-alloc has been moved to its own crate since it has been stable for some time

### Fixed

- Fix panic when using `alloy_primitives::utils::keccak256()`
- Proper encoding of tuples containing dynamic length types
- Add missing definitions in `export-abi` output
- Support for associated types in `export-abi`
- Disallow shadowing of constructor function selector
- Better sanitization of names in `export-abi` output
- Disallow `AbiType` definitions which shadow solidity reserved type names
- Fix panic when using `console!` macro in testing environment
- Allow parameterized traits with associated types
- Increase size of `ConstString` used to define potentially long `AbiTypes
- Support for solidity mapping types in `sol_storage!` macro

### Removed

- Removal of deprecateed code from previous versions
- Old inheritance model no longer supproted

## [0.9.2](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.9.2) - 2025-09-23

### Fixed

- Fix segfault when testing with the keccak function in alloy.

## [0.9.0](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/stylus-sdk-rs/releases/tag/v0.9.0) - 2025-05-20

### Changed

- Fix formatting by @amsanghi in #222
- Add Stylus constructors by @gligneul in #184
- first pass implementation of trait based inheritance by @rory-ocl in #223
- Fix Cargo Stylus Replay by @gligneul in #225
- Update CHANGELOG.md (main) by @gligneul in #228
- Remove mark_used function to reduce binary size by @gligneul in #235
- Port 0.8.3 changes to main by @gligneul in #231
- add StorageU96 int alias by @0xNeshi in #234
- Remove the HostIO-caching feature by @gligneul in #237
- Add a README to Stylus Test by @rauljordan in #239
- Be more strict with special function names by @gligneul in #242
- Resolve Audit Feedback Related to TestVM and Fallbacks by @rauljordan in #241

content.text:
I wrote the TSV to `/tmp/bench/notes/e2e-parts/g3.tsv`. It has one header and 48 data rows for `examples/erc1155/tests/erc1155.rs`, in list order. Every row has 7 columns, and the line numbers and names match `list.tsv` and the source.

- **SUCCESS:** 17
- **FAILURE:** 31, of which 1 is `return false (no revert)`
- **Expected errors in FAILURE rows:** `Erc1155::ERC1155InvalidReceiver` 10, `Erc1155::InvalidReceiverWithReason` 8, `Erc1155::ERC1155InsufficientBalance` 4, `Erc1155::ERC1155MissingApprovalForAll` 4, `Erc1155::ERC1155InvalidArrayLength` 3, `Erc1155::ERC1155InvalidOperator` 1.
- **Contract under test:** `Erc1155` for every row except the 8 burn tests, which say `Erc1155 (IErc1155Burnable)`. In the receiver-mock tests the mock is only a helper, not the target.
- **InvalidReceiverWithReason rows:** the expected column holds only that error type. The wrapped `Error("...")` message or `Panic(DivisionByZero)` is in the description. The panic code is actually checked there, because it is encoded into the expected message passed to `reverted_with`, not to `panicked_with`.

Unsure cases:
1. `is_approved_for_all_zero_address`: I marked it FAILURE, `return false (no revert)`, following the rule literally. Its only assertion is that `isApprovedForAll(alice, Address::ZERO)` returns false. Read loosely, it is a view call returning the default "not approved" state, so SUCCESS would also be defensible.
2. `set_approval_for_all`: I marked it SUCCESS. It does check that `isApprovedForAll` returns false, but only as the state after a successful revoke. Both `setApprovalForAll` transactions succeed and emit `ApprovalForAll`, so the false is not an unsuccessful return.

Nothing under `/tmp/bench/v030` was changed, and no other files were created.

#!/bin/bash
# D2-D4: for every example crate (examples/*/ and examples/basic/*/ with a [package] name):
#   - wasm-opt --enable-bulk-memory -O3 (same flags as scripts/bench.sh)
#   - raw and wasm-opt file sizes in bytes
#   - cargo stylus check -e https://sepolia-rollup.arbitrum.io/rpc --wasm-file <raw .wasm>
#     with `sleep 2` after each call, as scripts/check-wasm.sh does.
# Output: /tmp/bench/baseline/wasm/<crate_name>.{wasm-opt,check}.txt and wasm/sizes.tsv
RL=/tmp/bench/baseline/tools/rl.sh
SRC=/tmp/bench/v030
WASM=$SRC/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release
OUT=/tmp/bench/baseline/wasm
mkdir -p "$OUT"
TSV="$OUT/sizes.tsv"
printf 'example\tcrate\traw_bytes\twasm_opt_bytes\tstylus_check_exit\n' > "$TSV"

names=$(cd "$SRC" && for f in examples/*/Cargo.toml examples/basic/*/Cargo.toml; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && grep -q '^\[package\]' "$f" && grep -m1 '^name = ' "$f" | sed -E 's/^name = "(.*)"/\1/'
done)

for n in $names; do
  f=${n//-/_}
  raw="$WASM/$f.wasm"
  opt="$WASM/${f}_opt.wasm"
  if [ -f "$raw" ]; then
    rawb=$(stat -f %z "$raw")
    "$RL" "$SRC" "wasm-opt --enable-bulk-memory -O3 -o $opt $raw > $OUT/$f.wasm-opt.txt 2>&1"
    optrc=$?
    optb=$( [ -f "$opt" ] && stat -f %z "$opt" || echo NA )
    "$RL" "$SRC" "cargo stylus check -e https://sepolia-rollup.arbitrum.io/rpc --wasm-file $raw > $OUT/$f.check.txt 2>&1"
    chkrc=$?
    sleep 2
  else
    rawb=MISSING; optb=MISSING; chkrc=NA
    echo "$f: raw wasm missing" > "$OUT/$f.check.txt"
  fi
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(echo "$n" | sed 's/-example$//')" "$f" "$rawb" "$optb" "$chkrc" >> "$TSV"

#!/bin/bash
# Polls http://localhost:8547 with eth_chainId (via cast) until it answers, or until the limit.
# Usage: wait-rpc.sh [max_seconds]   (default 900)
MAX=${1:-900}
start=$(date +%s)
while true; do
  out=$(cast chain-id --rpc-url http://localhost:8547 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [[ "$out" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    echo "RPC_UP eth_chainId=$out (dec) elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))s"
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ $(( $(date +%s) - start )) -ge "$MAX" ]; then
    echo "RPC_TIMEOUT after ${MAX}s; last cast output: $out"
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 10
done

content.text:
I wrote the TSV to `/tmp/bench/notes/e2e-parts/g1.tsv`. It has 92 data rows, one for every listed test in `examples/erc4626/tests/erc4626.rs`, in list order.

- **SUCCESS:** 50
- **FAILURE:** 42 (12 `Erc4626::InvalidAsset`, 19 `PanicCode::ArithmeticOverflow`, the rest are other ERC4626, ERC20 or SafeErc20 errors)
- **`return false (no revert)`:** 0

**Checks:** every row has 7 fields and no description is over 160 characters. Columns 1–3 match the list exactly. A pattern scan of each test body for error assertions agrees with all 92 classes.

**Unsure:** none on classification. Three cases you should know about:
- **`withdraw::maintains_state_consistency_after_failed_withdrawal`:** it uses `expect_err` but never checks which error comes back. I classed it FAILURE and wrote "unspecified error (expect_err only; intended ERC4626ExceededMaxWithdraw)" in the expected column.
- **`preview_withdraw::reverts_when_result_overflows`:** despite the name, it calls `previewDeposit(U256::MAX)`, not `previewWithdraw`, which looks like a copy-paste bug in the test. The description says so.
- **`withdraw::reverts_when_withdrawing_from_zero_address`:** it asserts two failing calls, so the expected column lists both errors (`Erc4626::ERC20InvalidApprover; Erc4626::ERC4626ExceededMaxWithdraw`).

The 19 panic tests write `PanicCode::ArithmeticOverflow`, but the framework ignores that argument, so any "execution reverted" error would pass them. Their descriptions say "code not checked".

`contract_under_test` is `Erc4626` everywhere except `withdraw::reverts_when_transfer_fails`, which is labelled `Erc4626 (ERC20FailingTransferMock asset)`.

content.text:
I wrote `/tmp/bench/notes/e2e-parts/g2.tsv` with 64 data rows, one per listed test in `examples/erc721/tests/erc721.rs`, in list order.

- **Counts:** 22 SUCCESS and 42 FAILURE. 3 of the FAILURE rows are `return false (no revert)`: `sets_approval_for_all`, `is_approved_for_all_invalid_operator` and `supports_interface`.
- **Checks:** every line has 7 tab-separated fields, the longest description is 157 characters, and the file/line/test columns match `list.tsv` exactly. The file is plain ASCII with LF line endings.

Unsure cases. All of these are FAILURE only because the SUCCESS rule says a test may have "no error or false-return assertion"; judged by their main call, they test the success path:
1. `burns`, `burns_approved_token`, `burns_approved_for_all`: the burn succeeds. The only error assertion is the follow-up check that `ownerOf` reverts with `ERC721NonexistentToken` after the burn.
2. `token_of_owner_by_index_after_transfer_to_another_account`, `token_by_index_after_burn`: the transfers or burn and the lookups succeed. The test also checks that indexes which no longer exist revert with `ERC721OutOfBoundsIndex`.
3. `sets_approval_for_all` is the most debatable. Both `setApprovalForAll` calls succeed, and the `false` from `isApprovedForAll` is the expected state after revoking, not a failed call.
4. `supports_interface`: three interface IDs are asserted true. Only the invalid ID `0xffffffff` is asserted to return false.

If these should count as SUCCESS, it's 8 rows to flip, and the totals would become 30 SUCCESS and 34 FAILURE.

content.text:
I wrote `/tmp/bench/notes/e2e-parts/g7.tsv` with one header line and 48 data rows. It matches the filtered `list.tsv` exactly (same file, line, test, same order), and every row has 7 tab-separated columns. The longest description is 157 characters, and the file is ASCII with LF line endings.

- **Rows:** 48
- **SUCCESS:** 19
- **FAILURE:** 29
- **`return false (no revert)`:** 4. These are the two `returns_false_on_try_safe_transfer*` tests in `safe_erc20_address_with_no_code.rs` and the two in `safe_erc20_erc20_that_always_returns_false.rs`.

Unsure cases:
1. **`not_granted_roles_can_be_revoked` (access_control.rs:182):** I classified it SUCCESS. It does assert that `hasRole(ROLE, alice)` is false, but only as a setup check; the call under test, `revokeRole`, succeeds and the test asserts that no RoleRevoked event is emitted. A strict reading of the "asserts a call returns false" rule would make it FAILURE.
2. **All 3 tests in `safe_erc20_erc1363_no_return.rs` (lines 18, 48, 80):** I classified them FAILURE, but they only call `expect_err("should revert without reason")` and never check an error type. The expected column therefore says `any error (expect_err only, no type asserted)`. Also, despite the file name, they deploy the return-false mock (`erc1363_return_false::deploy`) and only use the no-return mock's interface to call it, so the no-return mock is never actually run. I named the contract under test after the mock that is really deployed.
3. **The 4 `return false` rows:** the test checks the false result indirectly, through the `False` event the example contract emits whenever the function returns false. I'm fairly confident these are right.

In the expected column, error names are copied exactly as each test writes them. Line 113 has `AccessControl::AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount`, while lines 240, 524 and 558 have the bare `AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount`; it is the same error type.

I wrote `/tmp/bench/notes/e2e-parts/g5.tsv` with 58 data rows: 20 SUCCESS, 38 FAILURE, and 2 rows marked `return false (no revert)`.

- **Checks:** the file/line/test columns match the list exactly and in list order (permit, erc20, wrapper, flash-mint). Every row has 7 fields, LF only, ASCII only, and the longest description is 143 characters. All 58 listed lines point at real `async fn` definitions, and there are no `mod` blocks in these files.
- **Repo:** I only read from `/tmp/bench/v030`. It is not a git repository, so I couldn't confirm "no changes" with git status.

Unsure cases:
- **`max_flash_loan_returns_zero_on_invalid_address` (FAILURE):** the call returns 0, not false. ERC-3156 says an unsupported token must return 0 instead of reverting, so I counted it as an "unsuccessful return value". I used the `return false (no revert)` label as instructed, even though the value is 0.
- **`max_flash_loan_return_zero_if_no_more_tokens_to_mint` (SUCCESS):** here 0 is the correct remaining capacity for a supported token, not an error signal. It could be argued FAILURE by analogy with the test above.
- **erc20 `supports_interface` (FAILURE, `return false (no revert)`):** classified by the false-return rule because it asserts `supportsInterface(0xffffffff)` is false. It also asserts true for three valid interface IDs.
- **erc20 `constructs` and `unpauses` (SUCCESS):** both assert `paused()` is false. I read that as a state check, not an unsuccessful return.
- **`should_not_deploy_capped_with_invalid_cap`:** the expected column is `ContractInitializationError`, because the `ERC20InvalidCap` check is commented out as a TODO.
- **Panic rows:** the two `PanicCode::ArithmeticOverflow` rows are written as in the test, but the framework never checks the code.

content.content:
### Reproducible `wasm-opt` optimization

For contracts that need a [Binaryen](https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen) `wasm-opt` pass to fit under the size limit, cargo-stylus can apply a **pinned** `wasm-opt` step as part of the build and **replay it identically during verification**, so the deployed bytes still verify reproducibly.

Declare a `[wasm-opt]` table in your `Stylus.toml`:

```toml
[wasm-opt]
version = "131"     # pinned Binaryen version (a plain version number; see the
                    # Binaryen releases and pin the one you validate against)
flags = ["-Oz"]     # passed verbatim to wasm-opt, in order
```

- **Opt-in and layered.** A contract is optimized only if its own `Stylus.toml` contains a `[wasm-opt]` table. In a workspace, a `[wasm-opt]` table at the workspace root provides shared defaults (`version`/`flags`) that opted-in contracts inherit; a bare `[wasm-opt]` table in a contract means "opt in and inherit the workspace recipe", and any field it sets overrides the default. For a single-contract project the lone `Stylus.toml` opts the contract in.
- **Reproducibility.** The version + flags are folded into the deployment's `project_hash`, and the reproducible Docker build installs the pinned `wasm-opt` automatically. Running `cargo stylus deploy`/`verify` without `--no-verify` (the default) needs no local Binaryen install.
- **Local builds.** Commands that build locally — `deploy`/`verify` with `--no-verify`, and `check`/`get-initcode`, which have no reproducible path — shell out to `wasm-opt` on your `PATH` and error if its version does not match the pinned one. For `deploy`/`verify`, prefer the reproducible (Docker) build rather than hand-installing a specific version.
- **Flags.** Flags are passed to `wasm-opt` verbatim and can change which instructions it emits, so choose flags that keep the output within Stylus's supported WebAssembly feature set; invalid output is rejected at activation.
- **`--wasm-file` bypasses wasm-opt.** Commands given a prebuilt Wasm via `--wasm-file` have no Stylus project to resolve a recipe from, so the `[wasm-opt]` table is not applied — optimize such files yourself before passing them in.

content.text:
I wrote the table to `/tmp/bench/notes/e2e-parts/g4.tsv`. It has 50 data rows plus the header, and the file, line and test columns match the list exactly and in the same order. 37 rows are SUCCESS and 13 are FAILURE; 4 of the FAILURE rows are `return false (no revert)`. Every row has 7 columns, the file is plain ASCII with LF line endings, and the longest description is 147 characters.

Cases I was unsure about:
- **`supports_interface` (erc1155-supply, erc1155-holder, erc721-metadata):** I marked these FAILURE, `return false (no revert)`, because each asserts `supportsInterface(0xffffffff)` is false. They also assert true for valid IDs, so a happy-path reading would make them SUCCESS.
- **`is_approved_for_all_zero_address`:** FAILURE, `return false (no revert)`. The call is made with a zero-address operator and returns false instead of reverting. The base erc1155 file pairs it with a revert test for the same input. Against that, it sits under a "Happy Paths" header and only reads default state.
- **erc1155-supply `constructs`, `burn`, `burn_with_approval`, `burn_batch`, `burn_batch_with_approval` and `set_approval_for_all`:** I kept these SUCCESS. They do assert a false from `exists()` or `isApprovedForAll()`, but I read that as a state check after a successful call. A strictly literal reading of "no false-return assertion" would make all six FAILURE.
- **`withdraw_to_success`, `burns`, `set_token_uri_before_mint` and `return_token_uri_after_burn_and_remint`:** FAILURE because each asserts `ownerOf` reverts with `ERC721NonexistentToken`, even though the main action succeeds. `withdraw_to_success` is FAILURE despite its name.
- **`error_when_to_is_zero` and `error_when_exceed_batch_size`:** expected is `ContractInitializationError`, the only thing the test asserts. The specific `ERC721InvalidReceiver` and `ERC721ExceededMaxBatchMint` checks are commented out as TODOs.
- **The two `mint_panics_*` tests:** I wrote `PanicCode::ArithmeticOverflow` as it appears in the test, but the framework ignores that code.

=== CHANGELOG head
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [v0.3.0] - 2025-09-10

> **Heads-up:** this is the production release after one alpha and one release candidate
> (`alpha.1`, `rc.1`). The items below aggregate the _user-facing_ changes
> since **v0.2.0**. For the step-by-step evolution, see the individual
> pre-release sections further down.

### Added

- **UUPS Proxy**: `UUPSUpgradeable` contract and `IErc1822Proxiable` trait for user-controlled upgradeable proxies.
- **Beacon Proxy**: `BeaconProxy` contract and `IBeacon` interface, supporting the beacon proxy pattern for upgradeable contracts.
- **Upgradeable Beacon**: `UpgradeableBeacon` contract, allowing upgradeable beacon-based proxies with owner-controlled implementation upgrades.
- **Enumerable Sets**: Generic `EnumerableSet` type with implementations for `Address`, `B256`, `U8`, `U16`, `U32`, `U64`, `U128`, `U256`.
- **Token Receivers**: `IErc1155Receiver` and `IErc721Receiver` traits with corresponding `Erc1155Holder` and `Erc721Holder` contracts.
- **Access Control Extensions**: `AccessControlEnumerable` extension that supports role member enumeration.
- **Enhanced SafeERC20**: Additional methods including `try_safe_transfer`, `try_safe_transfer_from`, and relaxed call variants.
- **Cryptography**: EDDSA (Ed25519) signature scheme, Twisted-Edwards Curves, and enhanced elliptic curve configurations (secp256k1, Baby Jubjub, Band
- **Precompiles**: Enhanced `Precompiles` trait with `p256_verify` wrapper function for ergonomic precompile invocation.
